title: Review a friend's React PR without sounding harsh
persona: Ananya, on a hackathon team with 2 friends
scenario: Your hackathon teammate (and friend) opened a PR with their first React component. It works, but it has 6 useState hooks instead of one useReducer, no key on a list, an inline function in JSX causing re-renders, and one of those hooks holds an entire API response when you only need 3 fields. You need to leave a code review that's technically right AND doesn't make them feel stupid in front of the other 2 teammates watching the PR.
badPrompt: do a code review of this react PR
badOutput: Code review: This PR has several issues. Multiple useState calls should be consolidated. Missing keys on list items. Inline functions cause re-renders. Storing the entire API response is wasteful. Please fix these before merging.

hints.title: Force the tone explicitly
hints.body: ‘Tone: warm peer, not staff engineer. Public PR comments others will read. Praise one thing first.’ Tone in code review is the whole game.

hints.title: Distinguish must-fix from nice-to-have
hints.body: ‘Tag each comment as blocker, suggestion, or nit.’ Friends respond very differently when you separate ‘must change’ from ‘might consider’.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, code review comments.
Anchor the relationship, friend on a hackathon team.
Surface that this is their first React PR, calibrates depth.
Force a warm peer tone, not staff-engineer.
Demand one thing praised first. Sets the tone.
Force the blocker/suggestion/nit tagging. Reduces friction.
Reference the other teammates reading. Public reviews need different tone than DMs.
Specify the structure, one comment per file/line, with tags.
Demand the ‘why’ on each comment. Code review without why is just opinion.

tipIfLow: Code review for friends fails when AI defaults to staff-engineer tone. The unlock is naming the relationship (friend, hackathon, first React PR), forcing a warm peer voice, AND tagging blocker/suggestion/nit so they know what's actually required to merge.
goldPrompt: Act as a warm peer reviewer, NOT a staff engineer. I'm Ananya, hackathon. My friend opened their first React PR. Issues spotted: 6 useState (should be useReducer), no key on a list, inline JSX function causing re-renders, one hook holds an entire API response when only 3 fields are used. The other 2 teammates will read this PR. Output PR comments. Each comment tagged [BLOCKER], [SUGGESTION], or [NIT]. Lead with one genuine praise. For each issue, explain the why in 1 sentence and link a doc, not a lecture. Refuse to use 'obviously' or 'just'. Cap at 6 comments.
